Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The change affects stock simulation, geometry, and carried-fixture collision checks.

The change retains exact stock bounds and adds boundary subdivision. The tests cover contact, clearance, sub-pitch overlap, steps, and quarter turns. The posting test checks that a fixture collision blocks the program.

All checks ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-2144`. The trial merge with upstream main `57f2ffbbf` was clean. No GitHub runner was used.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --no-run` | Passed |
| Quick gate: sim, 43 test targets | 474 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored |
| Quick gate: motion, 1 test target | 1 passed, 0 failed |
| Quick gate: app, 52 test targets | 682 passed, 0 failed, 15 ignored |
| New `carried_boundary` suite | 4 passed |
| New `carried_fixture_side_contact` suite | 6 passed |
| `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed, zero warnings |

The quick gate passed all three steps. I repeated these mutation checks:

| Temporary mutation | Red result | Result after restoration |
|---|---|---|
| Restore upstream main's `fixture_carried.rs` | All 6 contact tests failed | All 6 passed |
| Drop retained history at the end of `air_outside_circle` | Cylinder contact test failed; 0.05 mm overlap returned `None` | Test passed |

I restored all source files after the probes. The review worktree has no source changes.

Requested before merge: none.

Notes:

- An extra probe that removed only `h.cylinder` passed the equator contact test. That test does not isolate cylinder curvature.
- No G-code, CL, or golden files changed. No golden comparison was required.
- No UI files changed. Screenshots were not required.
- Open stock meshes and raw grids retain the stated sampling limit. Release-only tests were not run.
- I checked the laws against upstream main's current `AGENTS.md`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 39e3ec271a79ae6a998a311bf6b3d20956e4b901 -->

**Verdict: clean.** This is the independent second review under the safety floor. It is not the author's review. I built and tested the final head in a local worktree. The branch trial-merges cleanly with current main.

What I ran (debug tier; the ignored heavy lanes did not run):

- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --test carried_boundary`: 4 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test carried_fixture_side_contact`: 6 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test carried_fixture_guards`: 8 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --lib`: 184 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: no warnings.

What I verified in the code:

- The new checks only add to the old verdict. `penetration` and `mesh_penetration` pass the coarse result into `boundary_box_penetration` and `boundary_mesh_penetration`. Those functions only raise the depth through `take_max`. No path lowers a reported hit.
- The centre-column fallback in `scan` stops only when continuous history exists. The boundary scan then reads the same history over the whole box with exact spans. The routed `material` reads report true point spans, not the wider column hull. This removes phantom material over an air gap; it cannot remove real material.
- Sub-pitch side-face and step contact resolves to 1e-3 mm (box) and 2e-3 mm (mesh) leaf tiles, against a 1 mm grid pitch. Steel up to one pitch into a face no longer passes as contact.
- Degenerate input gives a conservative result, not a wrong pass. Non-finite bounds and an exhausted budget give `RegionStock::Unread`, which keeps the reach. An open model mesh where `FixtureMesh::build` fails keeps the old column law, as the PR body states.
- No `unwrap`, `expect`, or `panic!` in the source diff. Exact float tests on frame and motion values guard fast paths only; each one falls through to the conservative subdivision path. Index math clamps before use.
- 400-line law: the largest changed file is 375 lines. Test placement: each test file imports what its crate defines. Provenance lines, the decision record, and the `Changelog:` line are present. No process file, CI file, or snapshot PNG changed.

Notes (not blockers):

- On the box path the erosion tolerance is 1e-9 mm. A steel sliver thinner than one leaf, between the five sample lines, can still pass. That gap is three orders finer than the one-pitch gap this PR closes. `docs/decisions/1580-side-face-contact.md` states the leaf limit.
- In `cut_effect`, the `offsets.iter().any` containment test relies on this law: every eroded point of the box lies inside every stencil-shifted copy of the box. I checked that reading against the arc-sweep and side-turn tests.
